5: ## Product Boundary
6: 
7: STDO 3 is a specification methodology realised as documents. It defines purposeful construction and evaluation for actors with finite context, attention, time and capability.
8: 
9: The structure distinguishes general foundations, Spec Method as one particular methodology, and optional domain profiles and operational realisations. Proposed algorithmic, informational and computational interpretations are orthogonal concerns.
10: 
11: The source project owns one common WHAT. Codex and Claude are independent build tenants supplying HOW and documentary implementations. Their organisation, wording and encodings may differ while their accepted outputs satisfy the same common contract and independently specified expectations.
12: 
13: The method semantics expressed by tenant documents are distinct from the common construction specification that governs those documents. A tenant design is not a replacement Product definition. a_c interpretations and tools retain separately owned dependency and proof identities.
14: 
15: ABG, HoG and application workflow runtimes remain outside this Product. A worked application, Hello World or Data Mapper is an external example or test subject. Its particulars cannot become generic method functionality by precedent.
16: 
17: ## Construction Authority

18: A finite actor, human or model, should recover from these documents what it
19: needs to do bounded governed work with less interpretive reconstruction than
20: the 2.5.1 corpus requires, and nothing the 2.5.1 corpus requires should be
21: lost without an explicit disposition. Every clause therefore carries two
22: things: the principle that requires it, and its disposition relative to the
23: rc.2 clause it conserves, reframes or supersedes.
24: 
25: ## Tiers and files
26: 
27: | Tier | File | Carries | Requiring principles |
28: |---|---|---|---|
29: | 1 | [FOUNDATIONS.md](../standards/FOUNDATIONS.md) | ontology, the commitments as law, the algebra of composition and conservation, hypotheses | P0–P6 |
30: | 1 | [CALCULUS.md](../standards/CALCULUS.md) | the bounded step: intake, context construction under an envelope, grant, output; the result algebra; totality dispositions; refinement; work state and restart; cost and proportionality; reuse | P0, P4b, P5 |
31: | 1 | [EVALUATION.md](../standards/EVALUATION.md) | claims, evidence, independent assessment, review results, acceptance, conformance of realisations, method self-qualification and recoverability | P6, P1 |
32: | 2 | [SPEC_METHOD.md](../standards/SPEC_METHOD.md) | the particular method: constitutional chain, one WHAT and tenant HOWs, outcome conservation, change classes and re-entry, activation roles, checkpoints, release lineage | P2 with the tier-1 documents |
33: | 2 | [CONFORMANCE.md](../standards/CONFORMANCE.md) | the counterexample and trial cases the method must pass, with independently specified expectations | P6 |
34: | 3 | [PROFILES.md](../standards/PROFILES.md) | how software design, graph execution, UX and world-model profiles import the core and what stays out of it | P0 boundary |
35: | route | [README.md](../standards/README.md) | learn, apply, review and machine routes; document map | recoverability (derived from P0) |
36: 
37: Seven files. The 2.5.1 corpus has 52 standards members; the contraction is
38: by import and derivation, not by dropping obligations. Glossary and compressed
39: views are derived from these files later, never authored separately.

git_excerpts.text:
10: ## Library Before Instances
11: 
12: Use one definition of each shared transformation family. An instance binds a
13: purpose, subject, basis, required relations, responsibility and permitted effects.
14: Different instances do not require different mechanisms merely because their
15: names, inputs or owner roles differ. A new primitive is justified only by a
16: material semantic, authority, effect or failure distinction that the existing
17: definitions cannot express without losing the outer contract.
18: 
19: | Shared family | Performed relation | Preserved distinctions |
20: |---|---|---|
21: | Bind | Recover the exact current work subject, governing contract, role and live authority. | Purpose, identity, state, evidence and permission. |
22: | Acquire | Obtain sufficient material context or return unsupported acquisition/fit. | Source owner, exact selector, authenticity, availability, completeness and coupled invariants. |
23: | Transform | Produce bounded output/effects inside an admitted contract. | Original input/producer, actual effects, output and unresolved conditions. |
24: | Evaluate | Judge an exact predicate using sufficient admissible evidence. | Candidate, observation, judgment, assessor and required independence. |
25: | Conjoin | Combine compatible applicable results without losing failures or coverage. | Original citations, known failures, uncovered requirements, incompatible basis and uncertainty. |
26: | Dispose | Select the next already-authorized action from current state and result pressure. | Evaluation versus decision, repair owner, continuation, yield, stop and exhausted authority. |
27: 
28: These are proposed library relations, not new runtime APIs or universal required
29: serialized records. Bind/acquire/evaluate can involve I/O in a computational
30: realization; informational contracts do not make those operations cost-free.
31: Internal probabilistic solution strategy remains the worker's HOW. Pure helpers
32: can be shared without combining semantic owners or independent assessments.
33: 
34: Retain U (purpose), O (object/current state), κ (interpretation context), Σ
35: (common WHAT), algorithmic descriptions, informational interpretations and
36: computational realizations over architecture H as simultaneous views. They are
37: not sequential development phases. Publish only the supported categorical
38: fragment from C1; broader equivalence, hardware metrics, statistical Markov
39: structure and HoG monadic binding remain separately scoped research claims.
40: 
41: ## Proposed Canonical Document Owners
42: 
43: Document names and grouping are Codex HOW. Common acceptance depends on behavior,
44: not these filenames. The first thread creates only its necessary clauses and
45: source routes. Later threads extend the same owners rather than starting another
46: parallel rule set for each observation.
47: 
48: | Planned tenant document | Owns | Imports instead of duplicating |
49: |---|---|---|
50: | standards/FOUNDATIONS.md | Interpretation, purpose, scoped objects, supported algebraic accounts and explicit open hypotheses. | Accepted C1 arguments and exact recovered source. |
51: | standards/SPEC_METHOD.md | Intent/Product/common WHAT/HOW derivation, realization boundaries and composition obligations. | Foundations; domain-specific design profile; work/evidence contracts. |
52: | standards/WORK_METHOD.md | Bound activation, sufficient context, execution/effect observation, current-state continuation and next-action disposition. | Evidence result algebra and governing WHAT/authority. |
53: | standards/EVIDENCE_METHOD.md | Claim/evidence/assessment boundaries, authentication, applicable independence and truthful conjunction. | Scoped identity/basis; qualification acceptance contract. |
54: | standards/QUALIFICATION_METHOD.md | Claim-appropriate actual-use evidence, operational claims, dependency, successor and release/adoption boundaries. | Work and evidence meanings; separately owned a_c mechanics. |
55: | standards/profiles/ | Optional software design, graph execution, work records and world-model contracts. | Core obligations; each profile's domain-owned meaning. |
56: 
57: Ticketing is a work-record realization when selected, not a prerequisite to every
58: direct bounded action. Graph traversal supplies a computational realization;
59: a graph's admitted validation can be reused on the same predicate and basis while
60: dynamic input/binding admission stays current. Operational state and evidence
61: ownership are selected by the profile; recovery does not require all history in
62: working memory. A deployment/UAT fixture is a test subject, never a core feature.
63: 
64: A published entry and responsibility views route a reader to these owners. A view
65: may be a sufficient projection for its declared claim; it cannot become rival
66: authority. RF-017 overlap stays when it supplies independent evaluation or a
67: different necessary evidence/capability altitude. UP-014 contracts duplicated
68: meaning and needless reconciliation, not every repeated explanation.

git_excerpts.text:
118: Status: PROPOSED on branch `common/c3-contract` for Jim's review. Nothing here is selected until he accepts it; the C3 checkpoint stays NOT_SELECTED in [GOALS](GOALS.md) until then. Where this section fixes C2 matters (acceptance criteria, audiences), it proposes them for the same decision.
119: 
120: Outcome. Each tenant produces a candidate for the target version: its foundational axioms and the full predecessor corpus restated on them per the [standalone successor requirement](requirements/README.md#standalone-successor-requirement), with every row of [PREDECESSOR_CLAIMS.md](requirements/PREDECESSOR_CLAIMS.md) carrying one UP-015 disposition and a successor locus, and with projected reference frames as the activation unit. The predecessor cut stays immutable and operative as builder until a release decision; it is not a component of the successor.
121: 
122: Frontier. The Executive holds `U0` = every `unresolved` row of PREDECESSOR_CLAIMS.md for the tenant, plus every evaluation the contract below requires that is not closed on the current basis. Each tenant declares its own member list and a map from every rc.2 member to the tenant members that receive it. The map is part of the tenant's frontier record and is reviewed with the first member.
123: 
124: Tier obligations. A tenant's organisation and wording are its own; what each tier owes is common:
125: 
126: | Tier | Owes | Receives from the predecessor |
127: |---|---|---|
128: | foundations | ontology, principles with standing, result algebra, the reference frame as a first-class object, bounded activation, work state, evidence and authority law | AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS, REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD, IDENTITY_METHOD, the generic law of SPEC_METHOD and RELEASE_METHOD |
129: | Spec Method | constitutional chain, requirements and design law, work carriers and triage, assurance and testing law, change classes and re-entry, release mechanics | SPEC_METHOD, TICKET_METHOD, DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD generic law, RELEASE_METHOD |
130: | profiles | realisation law that imports the tiers above and restates its own predecessor member in full | ODD_METHOD, TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE_PROFILE, UX_METHOD, WORLD_MODEL_METHOD, DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD realisation law, STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE frame catalogues and Executive law |
131: | guides | posting, writing, glossary | POSTING_GUIDE, WRITING_GUIDE, GLOSSARY_GUIDE |
132: | packaging | manifest, schemas, templates, compressions or their successor, bootstrap, plugin | the non-standard members; disposition may stay `unresolved` during construction and must close before an RC cut |
133: 
134: Activation unit. Each tenant publishes projected reference frames, one per selected task, from its restated corpus (a_c projections or an equivalent the tenant declares). A frame carries the clauses an actor needs for that task and nothing else. A frame, with its subject, is what any actor is activated on. Context is measured in bytes before the actor reads anything and recorded with the activation.
135: 
136: Audiences and tasks (PROPOSED selection of the open owner decision). Audiences: a fresh model actor activated on one frame against a declared subject; a human method owner reading by route; the Writer, Reviewer and Executive actors constructing or assessing the successor itself. Assumed knowledge: none beyond the activated frame and the subject; during construction, the installed predecessor for source routes. Tasks: do a bounded piece of work; resume work another actor left; review work; decide acceptance or release; apply a profile; construct or assess a successor member.
137: 
138: Executive loop. Existing authority is this contract and the ticket. The Executive selects the smallest dependency-ready set `M` from the frontier, normally one member or one declared cone, and activates one Writer per element with the UP-020 intake: exact outcome and checkpoint, the rows in scope, governing invariants, grant and write territory, evidence obligations, exclusions, stop and re-entry conditions, the context, wall and spend envelope, and the exact bounded action. The Writer returns one closed work result: `candidate_ready` with transition evidence (the restated text, its dispositions, its frames, its measured activations), `refused`, `incomplete` or `re_entry_requested`. The Executive evaluates the result, activates the Reviewer for every `candidate_ready` (independent review is required for every member), consumes the Reviewer's closed result, applies the disposition grant above, has the common pen ledger the decision in the ticket, and issues the next already-authorised activation. The Executive activation holds no write grant and never mutates ticket, candidate, common or worktree bytes; a same-actor role change is ledgered by the pen before the effect, and the actor is no longer Executive for that effect.
